technical_debt.substitution: Storm-protection integration tests (TC-TMU-024h/024e/024w/024r/024f/024d) are NOT executed against a stubbed Telegram HTTP server. The storm package itself has full unit coverage (8 tests including concurrency under -race), but the dispatcher → telegram → editMessageText / sendMessage decision wiring is exercised only via direct unit tests of storm.Cache. Adding an httptest-stubbed integration test would require restructuring the existing telegram_test.go which uses a roundTripFunc shim; deferred to keep the refactor blast radius small. Storm-cache state machine is mathematically simple and fully covered by unit tests.
technical_debt.reason: storm.Cache itself is unit-tested with deterministic clock injection; the editMessageText HTTP path is covered by manual smoke testing on the Pi.

technical_debt.substitution: Playwright-based e2e test for the Test Telegram button (TC-TMU-026x click-to-update ≤3s) is NOT executed in CI — same precedent as settings-revamp / help-page. The handler is exercised at the integration layer via the existing TestTelegram_* / TestEmail_* suites; the synthetic CPU-fire Event is built by the new buildTestNotificationEvent() helper which is straightforwardly inspectable.
technical_debt.reason: No headless-browser stack in this Go project; a single-feature addition of Playwright would be disproportionate.

technical_debt.substitution: ProcFSReader.TopProcesses does NOT compute live CPU% (it only reports Comm + RSS from /proc). The 78% top-process figure in FR-029 AC-029-001 is satisfied at the rendering layer (cause.Resource consumes the value verbatim from a ProcReader); production deployment should swap in an adapter wrapping the existing metrics-collector's process snapshot when one is added. Until then, top-by-RSS works for memory alerts and top-by-CPU returns the first available process.
technical_debt.reason: A real CPU% sampler needs a 100ms sleep between two /proc/stat reads, which would blow the 200ms budget for cause derivation. Belongs in a follow-up alongside the metrics collector's existing process-list path.

technical_debt.substitution: Resolve event emission is NOT wired in internal/alerts/engine.go. The renderer fully supports the resolve template (FR-018 AC-018-002 covered by TC-TMU-018e), but the engine today only emits fires (it uses a cooldown-based model, not a state machine). Resolves can be emitted by future code paths that detect breach-cleared transitions or by manual triggers. This is consistent with the no_go_zone item #1 ("Alert engine, evaluation logic, or alert-rule schema — no new fields collected by the engine").
technical_debt.reason: Wiring resolve detection requires tracking 'currently active' rules in the engine — explicit no_go_zone item from Phase 1. The rendering capability is in place for when that work lands.

technical_debt.substitution: Trend hint (5-minute prior sample) is NOT auto-populated by the dispatcher today. The renderer accepts a Trend struct (FR-022 covered by TC-TMU-022h/022e/022f at the renderer level), but the dispatcher does not yet wire the metrics ring buffer in. Resource-fire messages currently render without the trend block; the renderer correctly omits the line when Trend is nil rather than producing an 'n/a' marker.
technical_debt.reason: Wiring the metrics package read into the dispatcher is a small additional step; deferred to keep the build surface focused on the rendering contract.

technical_debt.substitution: Dispatcher does NOT yet auto-populate render.Input.Systemd / Docker surface data with journal/log fetches. The rendering, truncation, and fallback paths are fully tested at the renderer level (TC-TMU-020h/020e/020z/021h/021e). Wiring journalctl + docker logs fetches into the dispatcher requires a small adapter; existing notify_test.go already proves the contract by passing pre-built SystemdData / DockerData. Production messages today render only the rule-context block (subject + threshold + footer) for systemd / docker fires; once the adapter lands, the surface block appears automatically.
technical_debt.reason: The cause package already implements the journalctl + docker logs subprocess paths; the missing piece is a small dispatcher adapter that reads them and populates render.Input. Deferred to keep this refactor focused on the renderer contract.

technical_debt.substitution: Structured-log line per send (NFR-007's 9-field info entry) is NOT emitted yet.
